# BR-002 — Sequence numbers

## Goal
Let users number files while renaming, e.g. `IMG_4411.jpg` → `Trip_001.jpg`.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC-1: `Rename-ByPattern` gets a `-Sequence` switch. When set, the token `{n}` in `-Replacement` is replaced by a running number starting at `-Start` (default 1), zero-padded to `-Pad` digits (default 3).
- AC-2: Files are numbered in ascending order of their current name (ordinal, case-insensitive), so the result is deterministic.
- AC-3: Without `-Sequence`, `{n}` is left as literal text (backward compatible with BR-001 behaviour and tests).
- AC-4: Tests in `tests/Sequence.Tests.ps1` cover AC-1 to AC-3; all BR-001 tests still pass.

## Scope
- `src/BatchRename.psm1`
- new file `tests/Sequence.Tests.ps1`

## Out of scope
- Changing `scripts/*.ps1`.

## Verification
- `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/build.ps1`
- `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/test.ps1`
# PLAN

## Understanding
Add sequence numbering to `Rename-ByPattern` in `src/BatchRename.psm1`. A new `-Sequence` switch makes the function replace the token `{n}` in `-Replacement` with a running number for each file. The number starts at `-Start` (default 1) and is zero-padded to `-Pad` digits (default 3). For example, `IMG_4411.jpg` becomes `Trip_001.jpg`. Matched files are numbered in ascending order of their current name, using an ordinal, case-insensitive comparison, so the result is deterministic. Without `-Sequence`, `{n}` stays as literal text and BR-001 behaviour and tests are unchanged. A new test file, `tests/Sequence.Tests.ps1`, covers AC-1 to AC-3 using only the dependency-free helpers `Assert-Equal`, `Assert-True` and `New-TestFolder`. `scripts/*.ps1` is not changed.

## Files likely involved
- src/BatchRename.psm1
- tests/Sequence.Tests.ps1

## Steps
1. In `Rename-ByPattern`'s `param()` block, add `[switch]$Sequence`, `[ValidateRange(0, [int]::MaxValue)][int]$Start = 1` and `[ValidateRange(1, 9)][int]$Pad = 3`. Keep the existing parameters unchanged.
2. Right after the `$files = @(Get-ChildItem ... | Where-Object ...)` line, sort `$files` by name with an ordinal, case-insensitive comparison: `$keys = [string[]]@($files | ForEach-Object Name); [System.Array]::Sort($keys, $files, [System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)`. Do not use `Sort-Object`, because it compares by culture. Sort in every mode; it only fixes the order, so BR-001 results are unchanged.
3. Before the `$plan = @(foreach ...)` loop, set `$n = $Start`. Inside the loop, before `[regex]::Replace`, build the per-file replacement: `$rep = $Replacement; if ($Sequence) { $rep = $Replacement.Replace('{n}', $n.ToString().PadLeft($Pad, '0')); $n++ }`. Then call `[regex]::Replace($file.Name, $Pattern, $rep)`. Increment the counter before the existing `continue` for unchanged names, so every matched file uses up exactly one number. Numbers longer than `-Pad` digits are not truncated.
4. Update the comment-based help `.SYNOPSIS`/add `.PARAMETER` notes briefly describing `-Sequence`, `-Start`, `-Pad` and the `{n}` token (match existing terse style).
5. Create `tests/Sequence.Tests.ps1` in the same style as `RenameByPattern.Tests.ps1`, using fresh `New-TestFolder` folders:
  (a) AC-1/AC-2 defaults: files `IMG_4411.jpg`, `img_3000.jpg`, `IMG_0002.jpg`, plus `notes.md`, which does not match. Run with `-Pattern '(?i)^img_\d+' -Replacement 'Trip_{n}' -Sequence`. Expect IMG_0002→Trip_001.jpg, img_3000→Trip_002.jpg, IMG_4411→Trip_003.jpg; the files exist on disk and `notes.md` is unchanged.
  (b) AC-2 ordinal, case-insensitive order: files `b.txt`, `A.txt`, `file10.txt`, `file9.txt`. Run with `-Pattern '^.*(?=\.txt$)' -Replacement 'x{n}' -Sequence -Pad 1`. Expect A→x1, b→x2, file10→x3, file9→x4. A case-sensitive sort would put `A` differently, and a natural sort would put `file9` before `file10`.
  (c) AC-1 `-Start 7 -Pad 2`: two files become `_07` and `_08`. Also `-Start 100 -Pad 2` gives `100`, with no truncation.
  (d) AC-1 with `-WhatIf`: the returned objects show the numbered names, and the files on disk are unchanged.
  (e) AC-3: no `-Sequence`, file `a.txt`, `-Pattern '^a' -Replacement 'b{n}'`. Expect the new name `b{n}.txt` on disk. Passing `-Start`/`-Pad` without `-Sequence` also leaves `{n}` as literal text.
  In every case, find results by OldName or sort by OldName before asserting.
6. Run `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/build.ps1` and `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/test.ps1`. Both must exit 0, and the BR-001 tests must still report `ok`.

## Validation
- AC-1: Sequence.Tests.ps1 cases (a), (c) and (d) check that `{n}` is replaced by the zero-padded running number, using the default Start=1/Pad=3 and the custom values Start=7/Pad=2 and Start=100/Pad=2, both on disk and under `-WhatIf`.
- AC-2: Case (b) checks ordinal, case-insensitive numbering order (A before b; file10 before file9). Case (a) checks mixed-case IMG/img ordering.
- AC-3: Case (e) checks that `{n}` stays literal without `-Sequence`. The existing tests/RenameByPattern.Tests.ps1 and SafeFileName.Tests.ps1 pass unmodified.
- AC-4: `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/test.ps1` exits 0 with 'all tests passed'. `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/build.ps1` exits 0 and reports that both functions are exported.

## Risks
- `[System.Array]::Sort($keys, $items, $comparer)` overload resolution in PowerShell: it should bind to the non-generic `Sort(Array, Array, IComparer)`. If binding fails, fall back to `$files = @($files | Sort-Object { $_.Name.ToUpperInvariant() } -CaseSensitive -Culture '')`, or to a `List[object]` with an explicit comparison. Note that invariant culture is still not strictly ordinal, so Array.Sort is preferred.
- When `$files` is empty, the key/item arrays have length 0. Array.Sort handles this, but it must not throw under StrictMode Latest; wrapping in `@()` guards this.
- Numbered targets can collide with existing files, e.g. renaming into a folder that already has Trip_001.jpg, or reshuffling already-numbered files. The existing collision check throws before anything is renamed. This is safe but can surprise users, and a rename-in-place swap is not supported.
- A file whose computed name equals its current name still uses up a number (it is skipped after numbering). This keeps numbering tied to position in the sorted list.

## Assumptions
- Numbering covers every file that matches `-Pattern`, in sorted order, including files whose final name ends up unchanged.
- If `{n}` appears more than once in `-Replacement`, or the pattern matches more than once in one name, every occurrence in that file gets the same number.
- `-Start` must be >= 0 and `-Pad` must be in the range 1–9. Numbers wider than `-Pad` are left as they are, not truncated.
- `-Start`/`-Pad` are ignored without `-Sequence`.
- Sorting the matched files always, not only with `-Sequence`, is acceptable. It only makes the output order deterministic, and the BR-001 tests already sort the results.

## Open questions
- Should `-Start`/`-Pad` without `-Sequence` raise an error instead of being silently ignored? The plan ignores them.

# BatchRename — small PowerShell module used to learn the thien workflow.
Set-StrictMode -Version Latest

function ConvertTo-SafeFileName {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
      Replace characters that are invalid in Windows file names with '_' and trim spaces/dots.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param([Parameter(Mandatory, ValueFromPipeline)][string]$Name)
    process {
        $invalid = [System.IO.Path]::GetInvalidFileNameChars() + [char[]]'<>:"/\|?*'
        $chars = $Name.ToCharArray() | ForEach-Object { if ($invalid -contains $_) { '_' } else { $_ } }
        (-join $chars).Trim().TrimEnd('.')
    }
}

function Rename-ByPattern {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
      Rename matching files in one folder after checking all target names for collisions.
    .PARAMETER Sequence
      Replace {n} tokens with numbers in ordinal, case-insensitive file name order.
    .PARAMETER Start
      First sequence number (default 1). Ignored without -Sequence.
    .PARAMETER Pad
      Minimum sequence number width (default 3). Ignored without -Sequence.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Path,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Pattern,
        [Parameter(Mandatory)][AllowEmptyString()][string]$Replacement,
        [switch]$Sequence,
        [ValidateRange(0, [int]::MaxValue)][int]$Start = 1,
        [ValidateRange(1, 9)][int]$Pad = 3
    )

    $files = @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $Path -File -ErrorAction Stop |
        Where-Object { [regex]::IsMatch($_.Name, $Pattern) })
    $keys = [string[]]@($files | ForEach-Object { $_.Name })
    [System.Array]::Sort($keys, $files, [System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)
    $n = $Start
    $plan = @(foreach ($file in $files) {
        $rep = $Replacement
        if ($Sequence) {
            $rep = $Replacement.Replace('{n}', $n.ToString().PadLeft($Pad, '0'))
            $n++
        }
        $new = ConvertTo-SafeFileName ([regex]::Replace($file.Name, $Pattern, $rep))
        if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($new)) {
            throw "Empty target name for '$($file.Name)'"
        }
        if ($new -ceq $file.Name) { continue }
        [pscustomobject]@{ File = $file; OldName = $file.Name; NewName = $new }
    })

    foreach ($group in @($plan | Group-Object -Property NewName)) {
        if ($group.Count -gt 1) {
            throw "Name collision: '$($group.Name)' would be produced by $($group.Group.OldName -join ', ')"
        }
    }
    foreach ($item in $plan) {
        if (($item.NewName -ne $item.OldName) -and
            (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $Path $item.NewName))) {
            throw "Name collision: '$($item.NewName)' already exists"
        }
    }

    foreach ($item in $plan) {
        if ($PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($item.File.FullName, "Rename to $($item.NewName)")) {
            Rename-Item -LiteralPath $item.File.FullName -NewName $item.NewName -ErrorAction Stop
        }
        [pscustomobject]@{ OldName = $item.OldName; NewName = $item.NewName }
    }
}

Export-ModuleMember -Function ConvertTo-SafeFileName, Rename-ByPattern
# Defaults and preview: matched files get numbers in current-name order.
foreach ($preview in @($false, $true)) {
    $d = New-TestFolder
    $label = "sequence: defaults preview=$preview"
    foreach ($name in @('IMG_4411.jpg', 'img_3000.jpg', 'IMG_0002.jpg', 'notes.md')) {
        New-Item -ItemType File -Path (Join-Path $d $name) | Out-Null
    }
    $result = @(Rename-ByPattern -Path $d -Pattern '(?i)^img_\d+' -Replacement 'Trip_{n}' -Sequence -WhatIf:$preview)
    Assert-Equal "$label count" 3 $result.Count
    $expected = @{ 'IMG_0002.jpg' = 'Trip_001.jpg'; 'img_3000.jpg' = 'Trip_002.jpg'; 'IMG_4411.jpg' = 'Trip_003.jpg' }
    foreach ($old in $expected.Keys) {
        $item = @($result | Where-Object OldName -CEQ $old)
        Assert-Equal "$label $old count" 1 $item.Count
        Assert-Equal "$label $old target" $expected[$old] $item[0].NewName
        Assert-Equal "$label $old original" $preview (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $d $old))
        Assert-Equal "$label $old renamed" (-not $preview) (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $d $expected[$old]))
    }
    Assert-True "$label nonmatching unchanged" (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $d 'notes.md'))
}

# Lexical ordering, including cases that distinguish ordinal from culture sorting.
$d = New-TestFolder
foreach ($name in @('b.txt', 'A.txt', 'file10.txt', 'file9.txt', 'Z.txt', '_first.txt')) {
    New-Item -ItemType File -Path (Join-Path $d $name) | Out-Null
}
$result = @(Rename-ByPattern -Path $d -Pattern '^.*(?=\.txt$)' -Replacement 'x{n}' -Sequence -Pad 1)
$expected = @{ '_first.txt' = 'x1.txt'; 'A.txt' = 'x2.txt'; 'b.txt' = 'x3.txt'; 'file10.txt' = 'x4.txt'; 'file9.txt' = 'x5.txt'; 'Z.txt' = 'x6.txt' }
Assert-Equal 'sequence: ordinal count' 6 $result.Count
foreach ($old in $expected.Keys) {
    $item = @($result | Where-Object OldName -CEQ $old)
    Assert-Equal "sequence: ordinal $old" $expected[$old] $item[0].NewName
    Assert-True "sequence: ordinal target $old" (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $d $expected[$old]))
}

foreach ($start in @(7, 100)) {
    $d = New-TestFolder
    foreach ($name in @('a.txt', 'b.txt')) {
        New-Item -ItemType File -Path (Join-Path $d $name) | Out-Null
    }
    $result = @(Rename-ByPattern -Path $d -Pattern '^[ab]' -Replacement '_{n}' -Sequence -Start $start -Pad 2 | Sort-Object OldName)
    $expected = if ($start -eq 7) { @('_07.txt', '_08.txt') } else { @('_100.txt', '_101.txt') }
    Assert-Equal "sequence: start $start count" 2 $result.Count
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt 2; $i++) {
        Assert-Equal "sequence: start $start item $i" $expected[$i] $result[$i].NewName
        Assert-True "sequence: start $start target $i" (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $d $expected[$i]))
    }
}

# Sequence options do not expand tokens unless the switch is present.
foreach ($options in @(@{}, @{ Start = 7; Pad = 2 })) {
    $d = New-TestFolder
    New-Item -ItemType File -Path (Join-Path $d 'a.txt') | Out-Null
    $result = @(Rename-ByPattern -Path $d -Pattern '^a' -Replacement 'b{n}' @options)
    Assert-Equal 'sequence: literal count' 1 $result.Count
    Assert-Equal 'sequence: literal name' 'b{n}.txt' $result[0].NewName
    Assert-True 'sequence: literal target exists' (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $d 'b{n}.txt'))
}

# No matches must work with empty arrays under StrictMode.
$d = New-TestFolder
$result = @(Rename-ByPattern -Path $d -Pattern '^missing' -Replacement '{n}' -Sequence)
Assert-Equal 'sequence: empty match set' 0 $result.Count
# Dependency-free test runner (no Pester). Each tests/*.Tests.ps1 is dot-sourced and may use:
#   Assert-Equal <name> <expected> <actual>
#   Assert-True  <name> <condition>
#   New-TestFolder  -> a fresh empty temp directory (removed at the end)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$root = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
Import-Module (Join-Path $root 'src/BatchRename.psm1') -Force -DisableNameChecking
$script:failures = 0
$script:folders = @()
function Assert-Equal($Name, $Expected, $Actual) {
    if ($Expected -ne $Actual) { Write-Output "FAIL $Name expected=[$Expected] actual=[$Actual]"; $script:failures++ }
    else { Write-Output "ok   $Name" }
}
function Assert-True($Name, [bool]$Condition) {
    if (-not $Condition) { Write-Output "FAIL $Name"; $script:failures++ } else { Write-Output "ok   $Name" }
}
function New-TestFolder {
    $d = Join-Path ([System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) ("br-test-" + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N').Substring(0, 8))
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $d | Out-Null
    $script:folders += $d
    $d
}
try {
    Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $root 'tests') -Filter *.Tests.ps1 | Sort-Object Name | ForEach-Object {
        Write-Output "# $($_.Name)"
        . $_.FullName
    }
}
catch {
    Write-Output "FAIL (exception) $($_.Exception.Message)"
    $script:failures++
}
finally {
    $script:folders | ForEach-Object { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $_ -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
}
if ($script:failures -gt 0) { Write-Output "$($script:failures) test(s) failed"; exit 1 }
Write-Output 'all tests passed'
exit 0
